subject: Energy
title: Three Mile Island
description: A quick, practical guide to Three Mile Island.

hook.text: In March 1979, a partial meltdown struck Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania—the worst US nuclear accident.

buildup.text: A stuck valve caused coolant loss—operators misread instruments and made the situation worse by cutting emergency water.

discovery.text: About half the reactor core melted—but the containment building held, preventing significant radiation release.

twist.text: No deaths or injuries resulted—but public fear halted new US reactor construction for over 30 years.

climax.text: The accident led to major safety reforms—better training, instrument design, and emergency procedures worldwide.

punchline.text: No one was hurt—but nuclear power's reputation was.

quiz.question: What prevented major radiation release at Three Mile Island?
